errors.description: The IPSec pre-shared key cannot be cleared. Provide a new value to rotate it, or omit the field to leave it unchanged.

badRequest.description: Bad request — validation error. Common codes: `INVALID_FIELD` (schema or constraint violation), `IPSEC_SECRET_CLEAR_NOT_SUPPORTED` (explicit `null` sent for `ipsec.left.secret`).

errors.description: Hostname 'atlassian.com' is already assigned to another App.

conflict.description: Conflict — request is valid but cannot be processed due to current state. Common codes: `HOSTNAME_CONFLICT` — hostname already assigned to another App; `DEDICATED_IPS_LIMIT` — `dedicatedIps.enabled: true` quota exhausted; `MISSING_CATEGORY_NAME` — `categoryName` does not match any category returned by `GET /v1/categories`; `MISSING_SKU2_FOR_RISK_CONTROL` — risk controls require SKU2 entitlement not held by this customer; `MISSING_USER_GROUPS` — one or more assignment group IDs do not exist for this customer; `UNSUPPORTED_BARE_IP_IN_REFERENCED_VPN_ROUTE_IPSEC_CONFIG` — a `bareIps` subnet is not covered by the referenced gateway's IPSec tunnel `right.subnets`; `predefinedAppId` does not resolve to an existing template; for DELETE: gateway/grouped-gateway still referenced by an App, Grouped Gateway, or DNS Zone. Note: inaccessible gateway IDs in request bodies return `422 GATEWAY_NOT_FOUND`, not `409`.

createResponse.description: Resource created. Body contains `id` and `href`; `Location` header points to the new resource.

errors.description: One or more tenantIds do not belong to your organization.

forbidden.description: Forbidden — the caller's organization does not own one or more of the supplied `tenantIds`. JAG validates each `tenantId` against the JWT `organizationId`; any mismatch rejects the entire request.

serviceUnavailable.description: Service unavailable — transient server-side failure. For gateways: TRS failed to generate a unique 4-character hex ID after 10 attempts (extremely rare; the 16-bit ID space has 65,536 values and IDs are only exhausted under heavy load or ID leakage). Retry with exponential back-off; if persistent, contact Jamf support.

errors.description: Too many requests. Retry after the indicated period.

tooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Retry after the period indicated by `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying.

gatewayNotFound.summary: Gateway ID in request body not accessible to caller

errors.description: Gateway 'a1b2' does not exist or is not accessible to this customer.
All member gateways must have the same dedicatedIps.enabled value.
All member gateways must have the same tunnel type (all IPSec or all non-IPSec).
Grouped Gateway members must be dedicated gateways. Remove shared gateways from gatewayIds.

unprocessableEntity.description: Unprocessable entity — request is syntactically valid but violates a cross-field business constraint. Error codes: `GATEWAY_NOT_FOUND` — a gateway ID in `routing.gatewayId` or `gatewayIds` is not accessible to this customer (applies to Apps and Grouped Gateways; returns 422 rather than 404 because the ID is in the request body, not the path); `SHARED_GATEWAY_MEMBER` — one or more `gatewayIds` refer to shared (Jamf-managed) gateways, which cannot be members of a Grouped Gateway; `MIXED_DEDICATED_IPS_TYPES` — member gateways have mixed `dedicatedIps.enabled` values; `MIXED_TUNNEL_TYPES` — member gateways have mixed tunnel types (some IPSec, some non-IPSec). TRS `/external/v1` emits `422` directly for these violations.

ApiError.description: Standard error response body per ADG-54. Returned for all non-2xx responses.

errors.description: One entry per problem in the request.

description.description: Human-readable description for debugging. Do not display to end users.
description.example: Value is not a recognized category.

field.description: Name of the field that caused the error, if applicable.

id.description: ID of the object with the error, if applicable.

traceId.description: Trace ID for correlating this error across Tyk, JAG, and TRS. Include this value when reporting issues to Jamf support.

App.description: An App (Access Policy) defining ZTNA routing for a set of hostnames/IPs.

bareIps.description: IPv4 CIDR subnets (e.g. `192.168.1.0/24`). Duplicating a subnet across Apps returns 409.

hostnames.description: Hostnames/domains for traffic matching. Each entry must be a valid domain name, `"*"` (full-tunnel wildcard), or a wildcard prefix (`"*.example.com"`). Overlapping entries are rejected — e.g. `["*.example.com", "sub.example.com"]` returns `400` because `sub.example.com` is covered by `*.example.com`. Duplicating a hostname across Apps returns `409`.

name.description: Ignored when `predefinedAppId` is set — inherited from the predefined app template.

predefinedAppId.description: ID of the predefined SaaS app template (from `GET /predefined-apps`). Once set, cannot be changed or removed. When set, `name` and `hostnames` are inherited from the template; additional `hostnames` can still be appended.

AppCreateRequest.description: Request body for creating an App.

bareIps.description: IPv4 CIDR subnets (e.g. `192.168.1.0/24`). Duplicating a subnet across Apps returns 409.

name.description: Ignored when `predefinedAppId` is set — name is inherited from the template.

predefinedAppId.description: Optional. ID from `GET /predefined-apps`. Once set, cannot be changed or removed. When set, `name` and `hostnames` are inherited; additional `hostnames` can be appended. Presence indicates a Predefined (SaaS) App; absence indicates a Custom (Enterprise) App.

name.description: New name. Must be non-empty if supplied and `predefinedAppId` is not set — a blank string returns `400`. Ignored when `predefinedAppId` is set (name is inherited from the template). Omit to leave unchanged.

AppSecurity.description: Security controls applied to App traffic.

Assignments.description: User/group assignment rules for an App.

AssignmentsInclusions.description: Inclusion rules controlling who can access the App.

allUsers.description: `true` grants access to all users; `groups` array is then ignored.

groups.description: Device Group IDs (from the Device Groups API — JSC-71029). Used when `allUsers` is `false`. When `allUsers: false`, at least one group ID must be supplied — an empty `groups` array returns `400`.

CategoryName.description: App category name. Use the `displayName` field from `GET /v1/categories` — that endpoint is the authoritative source. The value must exactly match a `displayName` returned by `content-block-service`. Unknown values return `409 MISSING_CATEGORY_NAME` — the category list is server-owned and may change, so an unrecognized name is a state conflict, not a malformed request. TRS validates against `displayName` (e.g. `"Business & Industry"`), not the internal `name` (e.g. `"Category - Business & Industry"`).

tunnelState.description: IPSec tunnel health. Present only when the gateway has an IPSec configuration. `null` for non-IPSec gateways or before VSC reports the first tunnel status.

New and updated grouped gateways use one of the supported durations (`300`, `1800`, `3600`, `10800`, `28800`); grouped gateways created earlier may return a legacy value. Ignored for `RANDOM` and `NEAREST` strategies.

dnsIpResolutionType.description: DNS IP resolution preference. Optional. When omitted and `type=CUSTOM`, TRS defaults to `IPv6`. Explicitly set to `IPv4` if your network requires it. **Must be absent (or null) when `type=DIRECT`** — returns `400` if set.

gatewayId.description: ID of a Gateway or Grouped Gateway. Required when `type=CUSTOM`, must be null/absent when `type=DIRECT`. Gateway IDs are 4-character lowercase hex strings (e.g. `a1b2`); Grouped Gateway IDs are UUIDs (e.g. `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`).

type.description: `CUSTOM` routes traffic via a ZTNA gateway (`gatewayId` required). `DIRECT` uses default device routing (`gatewayId` must be null/absent). The internal TRS value `BLOCK` is not exposed in the public API.

groupIds.description: Must be a subset of `assignments.inclusions.groups` (or `allUsers: true`). A group ID may not appear in more than one routing override entry — returns `400` on conflict.

info.description: Manage ZTNA Gateways, Grouped Gateways, Apps, and Predefined Apps
info.title: Jamf ZTNA Public API (STAGE)

get.description:
List all Apps (Access Policies) for the tenant, paginated.


**Required Permissions:** `read:jsc:all`

post.description:
Create an App (Access Policy). Returns `201 {id, href}` + `Location` header.

**Required fields:** `categoryName`, `assignments`, `routing`.

**`name` required when `predefinedAppId` is absent:** If `predefinedAppId` is not set,
`name` must be non-blank — returns `400` otherwise. When `predefinedAppId` is set,
`name` is optional (inherited from the template).

**Full-tunnel restriction:** When `hostnames` contains `"*"` (wildcard — routes all traffic),
`security.riskControls.enabled` must be `false` — returns `400` otherwise.


**Required Permissions:** `create:jsc:all`

delete.description:
Delete an App (Access Policy). Returns `204` on success. Returns `404` if the App does not exist or is not owned by this customer. Returns `409` if deletion cannot complete due to a conflict.


**Required Permissions:** `delete:jsc:all`

404.description: App not found or not owned by this customer.

get.description:
Get a single App (Access Policy).


**Required Permissions:** `read:jsc:all`

404.description: App not found or not owned by this customer.

patch.description:
Partially update an App (Access Policy) (ADG-355).
All fields are optional — include only what you want to change.

Returns `404` if the App does not exist or is not owned by this customer.

TRS `/external/v1` performs server-side partial merge — reads the current App from
the database, merges the supplied fields, and persists atomically. No client-side
read-modify-write cycle.

**`name: ""`  is rejected.** Sending a blank string for `name` returns `400`
— when `predefinedAppId` is not set, `name` must be non-empty if supplied.
Omit `name` entirely to leave it unchanged.

**Full-tunnel restriction:** When `hostnames` contains `"*"` (wildcard — routes all traffic),
`security.riskControls.enabled` must be `false` — returns `400` otherwise.


**Required Permissions:** `update:jsc:all`

404.description: App not found or not owned by this customer.

get.description:
List dedicated Gateways for the tenant, paginated. Returns only customer-owned gateways. Each item includes datacenter, availability zones, IPSec configuration, and operational status.


**Required Permissions:** `read:jsc:all`

post.description:
Create a dedicated Gateway. Returns `201 {id, href}` + `Location` header.

`tenantIds` are validated against the caller's organization — returns **403** if any
tenant ID belongs to a different organization.

**Constraints:**
- `dedicatedIps.enabled: true` and `ipsec` are mutually exclusive → `400`
- `dedicatedIps.enabled: true` and non-empty `availabilityZones` are mutually exclusive → `400`
- Only **one** gateway with `dedicatedIps.enabled: true` is permitted per tenant (quota = 1).
  A second attempt returns `409 DEDICATED_IPS_LIMIT`. Contact your Jamf account team to increase this limit.
- Sending `ipsec.left.secret: null` explicitly returns `400 IPSEC_SECRET_CLEAR_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

**No idempotency key.** Gateway `name` is not unique-enforced — a timed-out POST that
succeeded server-side may create a duplicate gateway if retried. Verify via
`GET /ztna/gateways` before retrying a failed create.


**Required Permissions:** `create:jsc:all`

delete.description:
Delete a dedicated Gateway. Returns `204` on success. Returns `404` if the gateway does not exist or belongs to a different tenant — never `403`. Returns `409` if the gateway is still referenced by an App, a Grouped Gateway, or a DNS Zone — disassociate it first, then retry.


**Required Permissions:** `delete:jsc:all`

get.description:
Get a single dedicated Gateway. All fields are flat at the top level. Returns `404` if the gateway does not exist **or belongs to a different tenant** — never `403`, to avoid confirming the existence of gateways owned by other tenants (Gateway IDs are 16-bit enumerable; a `403` would be an existence oracle).

patch.description:
Partially update a dedicated Gateway. All fields are optional — flat body, no nesting.

Returns `404` if the gateway does not exist **or belongs to a different tenant** — never `403`,
to avoid confirming the existence of gateways owned by other tenants.

`tenantIds` are validated against the caller's organization — **403** on mismatch.
When `datacenter` changes, `availabilityZones` must match the new datacenter prefix
— returns `400` on mismatch.
Sending `ipsec.left.secret: null` explicitly returns `400 IPSEC_SECRET_CLEAR_NOT_SUPPORTED`
— omit the field to leave the existing secret unchanged.

**`contact: null` is rejected.** Setting `contact` to `null` in a merge-patch returns
`409` — the contact field cannot be removed from a dedicated gateway.

**`tenantIds: []` is rejected.** Setting `tenantIds` to an empty array returns `400`
— a dedicated gateway must always have at least one tenant (`minItems: 1` enforced by schema).

**Known limitation:** The server resolves the deployment ID via an internal GET before
issuing the PATCH. Concurrent modifications between the GET and PATCH may overwrite each
other. No optimistic locking is in place for this release — consider ADG-148
(`VersionId` + `409 OPTIMISTIC_LOCK_FAILED`) in a follow-up if this becomes a concern.

**Datacenter change is destructive:** Expect a connectivity outage while the gateway is
re-provisioned. `status.state` resets to `PENDING` immediately; `status.tunnelState` resets
to `null`; status records for the old datacenter are expired. `dedicatedIps.ips` are not
cleared immediately — treat them as unreliable until VSC completes provisioning in the new datacenter.


**Required Permissions:** `update:jsc:all`
